newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Sept 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
* Rising wages have accompanied a growing economy but there is little to indicate increased inflation, the Federal Reserve said.
* United Healthcare Corp won a contract from the American Association of Retired Persons worth over $4 billion yearly, underbidding Prudential Insurance Co of America.
* The Dow Jones industrial average rose to near its record high Wednesday, confounding analysts who see softer fundamentals than those behind recent bull moves.
* The Clinton Administration said it would start basing all environmental protection standards on the risks the pollution poses to children.
* Motorola's stock fell after the company warned of disappointing sales for cellular phones and other products.
* Studies point to a higher cost of trading on Nasdaq.
* New England Life Insurance plans to announce Thursday it bought a one-sixth stake in Meca Software for about $10 million.
* The Federal Trade Commission is expected to announce Thursday its formal approval of the merger between Time Warner Inc and Turner Broadcasting System Inc.
* Sun Communities Inc said it would offer cash for Chateau Properties, an alternative to its previous offer to pay in stock.
* International Business Machines Corp plans to announce Thursday it has developed software with improved speech-recognition capabilities.
